newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to send corn import mission to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Japan to send corn import mission to Argentina.

text.p: Japan's feed grain industry is to send a mission to Argentina next month with the aim of accelerating feed corn imports from the country in order to diversify corn supply sources, industry officials said on Thursday.
Japan has depended heavily on the United States for corn because of a Chinese export ban since 1994.
The 11-member mission will visit Argentine corn farmers, inspection facilities and ports from November 5-17, the officials said.
The mission will include senior corn traders of the National Federation of Agricultural Cooperative Associations, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Corp and Marubeni Corp.

"We were forced to depend on the U.S. too heavily for feed corn supplies after China suspended exports in late 1994. This is a vulnerable situation for major importer like Japan," said a member of the mission, who asked not to be identified.
"I'm not saying the U.S. is an unreliable exporter. But it makes great sense to diversify supply sources to other areas such as Argentina and South Africa," he said.
Japan imported 11,681,998 tonnes of feed corn in calendar 1995, Finance Ministry data showed. Of that, 11,590,623 tonnes, or 99.22 percent, came from the United States.
In the first eight months of this year, Japan bought 6,615,634 tonnes of corn and 99 percent of this came from the United States.
Corn is mainly used for making feed in Japan.
